Price is a big factor when you're looking for a data provider, whether you're a business looking to save some budget, or an independent researcher working with whatever funds you have. Of course, when you do spend your budget, you would want every penny of that budget spent to be worth it.

And so today, let's look into how much People Data Labs costs and what you'll get in return. But of course you can find that information on their [pricing page](https://www.peopledatalabs.com/pricing/person?ref=nubela.co) effortlessly. So here’s my proposition, along with their pricing, we will look what they offer for it, and if the investment is truly worth it.

For starters, here's a table showing [People Data Labs pricing](https://www.peopledatalabs.com/pricing/person?ref=nubela.co) plans.

| Plans | Price | Data Records |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | N/A | Up to 100 |
| Pro | $98/mo for person data | Starts at 350 credits ($0.28/ profile) |
|  | $100/mo for company data | Starts at 1,000 credits |
| Enterprise | Custom | Custom |

_**Note:** The \*FREE access is to their raw company database, which includes general company information like name, location, website info, etc. It **DOES NOT** contain any contact information. The data is quarterly updated and while it can be a good reference point, to get the actual fields that you need, you have to subscribe to one of their paid plans._

## What does People Data Labs do?

[People Data Labs (PDL)](https://www.peopledatalabs.com/?ref=nubela.co) is a data provider that helps companies build innovative and compliant data solutions at scale. They scrape publicly available data and work with third-party partners to get private data, then package it into datasets that customers can call using APIs.

Their data points offering are one of the largest in the market. They provide everything from name, location, contact information, social media details, and much more. Though they are guilty of breaking down one data point into many granular forms, which inflate the absolute quantity. For instance, let’s look at the job location address; which is split into 10 different fields! Examples include, `job_company_location_name`, `job_company_location_locality`, `job_company_location_metro`, `job_company_location_region`, etc.

Customers who opted for PDL’s service seem satisfied with what they get. Despite a few grievances, which I will discuss later, [People Data Labs Reviews](https://nubela.co/blog/people-data-labs-reviews/) are largely positive. Their commitment to quality and compliance is commendable. No doubt, they are setting some high industry standards.

## People Data Labs Pricing Plans

![People Data Labs Pricing](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcr0l9YAX2X5cHVCbPsbSfwkO6byZKDaYm5zwUR5Z05jFTKqT2DgKXZ5SUSzGKj38rfECtdTym8yIr9Gjber5yV7xWoksRLLprxOYCi85kRskHSyEVHY8f5frE7jGbQJCVnExosJP7EobGc-_1kFm841S3t?key=-xEtMtCS4WW6jckWwqYJfg)

The pricing model has three main subscription tiers available across each data plan type. For personal, company, or IP data plans, you can choose between Free, Pro, or Enterprise options.

Each tier provides access to different data fields, some of which are behind paywalls. The Free plan comes with limited field access, the Pro plan includes moderate access, and the Enterprise plan offers the most extensive field access. If your current plan doesn't cover specific fields you need, you can add them manually when upgrading from Free to Pro or even mid-cycle on the Pro plan. Keep in mind, though, that each additional field bundle you add is priced per credit.

See the field bundles pricing table below:

| Field Bundle | Type | Price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inferred Salary | Person | $0.01 |
| Inferred Years Experience | Person | $0.01 |
| Professional Social Network Connections | Person | $0.01 |
| Premium Resume Fields | Person | $0.03 |
| Ticker Information | Person | $0.01 |
| Premium Company Attributes | Person | $0.03 |
| Company Premium | Company | $0.10 |
| Inferred Revenue | Company | $0.03 |
| Funding Details | Company | $0.08 |

## People Data Labs API Pricing (Usage Based Model)

Apart from their subscription plan, there is a usage-based ['pay-as-you-go'](https://nubela.co/blog/people-data-labs-pricing/%3Chttps://support.peopledatalabs.com/hc/en-us/articles/25794271805211-Pricing%3E) model as well. The pricing plan allows you to choose only those APIs you need, based on three volume-based tiers. The [project team structure](https://www.virtosoftware.com/pm/project-management-team/?ref=nubela.co) can be crucial in determining which APIs are most relevant for your needs. You have the option to choose the amount of credits you purchase for each API and the silver lining is you're charged credits only when you get a successful match from the API.

Below, you'll find the pricing details for all the APIs provided by People Data Labs with a brief description. Be advised, it can get a bit complex as the pricing structure is super broken down (like their data points).

## Is People Data Labs worth it?

The short answer is no. For what you’re paying, there is a lot that could be better. And honestly, I’m still not fully on board with the price, either.

Why? Let me explain.

### 1\. Premium Pricing

People Data Labs has a proven track record of providing quality, accurate data. Their premium price is based on their high number of data points they provide and their brand exposure. But it is not all sunny in San Francisco. The high price is a recurring pain pont, particularly for startups and small businesses who value the data but can’t justify the high costs.

The cost per profile on the basic paid plan (Pro Plan) comes to $0.28; **ten times** the cost of other data providers like [ReachStream](https://reachstream.com/?ref=nubela.co) and [Proxycurl](https://nubela.co/proxycurl/?ref=nubela.co), which charge closer to $0.02 per profile. This stark contrast in pricing makes alternatives worth considering.

### 2\. Data Recency

People Data Labs’ datasets are updated monthly by default. That is all in good faith for fresh data, but there are a lot of reviews stating some data fields are not as recent. Now, I’m not here to judge, and I’d like to think their customer service steps up when issues arise. Still, wouldn’t it be reassuring to have a clear, written guarantee to data freshness? That would be great in an ideal world. Hmm. Think about it while you check out [Proxycurl’s Data Freshness Guarantee](https://nubela.co/blog/how-fresh-are-profiles-returned-by-proxycurl-api/) and decide what level of assurance works best for you.

### 3\. Steep Learning Curve

Most companies turn to data providers because they want them to handle the heavy lifting of data processing. You pay a price to make things convenient, so you can focus on things that actually need your attention. But if you’re having to dedicate a good chunk of your time just trying to know the platform, it defeats the purpose. A lot of customer were quick to point out the steep learning curve the platfrom has in their [reviews](https://nubela.co/blog/people-data-labs-reviews/). And when you’re paying the ‘People Data Labs’ price, you’re doubling down.

The intent here isn’t to question People Data Labs’ quality. By all means, they’re a reputable provider. But I beg to ask if their service is worth the price. For me, the answer is no. But don’t just take my word for it; check out [People Data Labs Reviews](https://nubela.co/blog/people-data-labs-reviews/). Real people sharing their real problems.

Now, ask yourself this,

**If you are paying a premium price, do you deserve these inconveniences? Moreover, is it necessary to pay a premium price, when other providers offer similar (or better) data quality at an economical price?**

The answer should be a resounding no.

## Is there a better option?

I am here to tell you People Data Labs isn’t the only major player in the market. Before anything, assess your data needs. After you are confident in what you’re looking for, the only thing left to do is browse your options. Check out [People Data Labs alternatives](https://nubela.co/blog/top-alternatives-to-people-data-labs/) to streamline your search. Here is a simmered down list:

1. **[Proxycurl](https://nubela.co/proxycurl/?ref=nubela.co) (Best Overall):** Proxycurl is a developer-focused company that provides a huge portfolio of API endpoints which scrape and enrich profiles. You can use Proxycurl's APIs flexibly and integrate them into any existing applications and workflows.

2. **[ReachStream](https://reachstream.com/?ref=nubela.co) (Cheapest):** ReachStream is a B2B sales and marketing data platform offering a simple, user-friendly platform where you can view unlimited contact and company profiles, firmographics, along with unlimited contact data updates for free.

3. **[Bright Data](https://brightdata.com/?ref=nubela.co) (Most Flexible):** Bright Data provides proxies for you to build your own scrapers. They also sell templates of scrapers that you can build on.

4. **[UpLead](https://www.uplead.com/?ref=nubela.co) (Highest Rated in G2):** UpLead is the highest rated B2B data provider in G2. They provide a clean prospecting list, which you can then plug into your CRM.


The best, complete alternative to People Data Labs, is Proxycurl. You can get everything you would from People Data Labs, at terms you can be satisfied with.

Here’s a direct comparison of People Data Labs and Proxycurl’s pricing:

## Final Thoughts

You do not have to break your bank to meet your data needs. While People Data Labs are renowned for their data accuracy and quality, their pricing sticks out like a sore thumb. And with enough alternatives to choose from, it’s good sense to do your due diligence before you commit. Save your budget, or rather spend it on other areas that need strengthening, without compromising on data quality or freshness.

Give [Proxycurl](https://nubela.co/proxycurl/?ref=nubela.co) a chance. Fulfill your data needs at a price you can be happy with. Whether you’re a developer seeking quick integration or a business in need of detailed professional data, Proxycurl delivers the same data points with far less hassle and cost.

## FAQs

#### Is People Data Labs free?

People Data Labs is NOT a free service. They do have a free plan, where you get access to their datasets and select fields, but to get your hands on their full product and fields, you need to subscribe to one of their paid plans. The pricing is customized based on data volume, access needs, and usage frequency. However, be advised, you CANNOT sign up using your personal email. Their system only allows sign ups through work emails.

#### Is People Data Labs legit?

People Data Labs is a reputed data provider in the industry. They have a solid customer rating of 4.6 out of 5. You can check out their in-depth review at [People Data Labs Review](https://nubela.co/blog/people-data-labs-reviews/).

#### Where do People Data Labs get their data?

People Data Labs has many data sources including open-source datasets, publicly available data, governmental public records and others. The gist is, they are all publicly available, and so are legally compliant.

#### Who owns People Data Labs?

People Data Labs is a privately held company. It was founded in 2015 by Sean Thorne and Joseph Drinkwater, who are still involved in the company's operations, aiming to revolutionize access to professional and B2B data.

#### Is People Data Labs a data broker?

People Data Labs is registered as a data broker under Texas law with the Texas Secretary of State (Texas SOS). More information about data broker registrants is available on the Texas SOS website.

#### What is People Data Labs data breach?

In October 2019, People Data Labs’s datasets were breached and were freely available on the Dark Web. 1.2 billion personal data records were vulnerable, almost every personal record the company held at the time.

# Profile Data APIs for Recruiting: 12 Providers Compared (2026)

Compare 12 profile data APIs for recruiting: People Data Labs, Apollo.io, ZoomInfo, and more. Self-serve from $39/mo to enterprise. Compliance guide included.

Sep 22, 2025 · Steven Lu

[Outreach](https://www.pin.com/blog/tag/outreach/) [Recruiting Tools](https://www.pin.com/blog/tag/recruiting-tools/)

![Profile Data APIs for Recruiting: 12 Providers Compared (2026)](https://pin-com.ghost.io/content/images/2026/03/profile-data-apis.png)

Updated At: Mar 14, 2026

> **TL;DR:** These APIs range from $39/mo self-serve (Snov.io, Coresignal) to $50K+/yr enterprise (ZoomInfo, Cognism). B2B contact data decays at roughly 2% per month - making fresh, API-accessible data critical. Recruiters who want enrichment without building anything should look at Pin (850M+ profiles, automated outreach, $100/mo).

Profile data APIs are programmatic interfaces that give recruiting teams and HR tech developers access to candidate information - job titles, employment history, emails, phone numbers, skills, and education - pulled from aggregated public data sources. The leading providers in 2026 include People Data Labs (1.5B+ profiles, from $98/mo), Apollo.io (275M+ contacts, from $49/mo), and RocketReach (700M+ profiles, from $33/mo). For recruiters who don't want to build anything, [Pin](https://www.pin.com/?ref=pin-com.ghost.io) offers 850M+ profiles with built-in outreach and scheduling starting at $100/mo - no API integration required.

Why does this matter now? The data enrichment market hit $2.37B in 2023 and is projected to reach $4.58B by 2030 at a 10.1% CAGR, according to [Grand View Research](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/press-release/global-data-enrichment-solutions-market?ref=pin-com.ghost.io) (2024). At the same time, the legal landscape has shifted dramatically. Proxycurl - a $10M ARR data provider - shut down in July 2025 after a LinkedIn lawsuit. Clearbit's free tools were sunset when HubSpot absorbed the product. And CCPA fines for mishandling job applicant data jumped to $7,988 per intentional violation.

This guide covers everything you need to evaluate and select these APIs: provider comparisons, pricing breakdowns, compliance requirements, and the market shifts reshaping the industry. If you're looking for specific API-by-API rankings, see our [developer guide to people search APIs](https://www.pin.com/blog/best-people-search-apis/?ref=pin-com.ghost.io). If you only need email lookup tools, check our [email finder tools comparison](https://www.pin.com/blog/best-email-finder-tools-recruiters/?ref=pin-com.ghost.io).

## What Are Profile Data APIs?

A profile data API is a software interface that returns structured candidate information when you query it with an identifier - a name, email address, LinkedIn URL, or company domain. The API responds with a JSON payload containing whatever the provider has aggregated: current job title, employer, work history, education, skills, contact details, and sometimes social profiles.

Think of it as a programmable lookup service. You send a request with a few known data points about a person, and the API fills in the rest. This is different from a people search engine (which provides a user interface for manual searches) or a contact finder tool (which specifically surfaces emails and phone numbers). These APIs return the full professional profile as structured data your software can process.

### How Profile Data APIs Work

Most providers aggregate their data from multiple sources: public web pages, business registrations, government records, social media profiles, job postings, and data partnerships. The aggregation process involves crawling, entity resolution (matching records from different sources to the same person), and data cleaning.

When a developer makes an API call, the typical flow works like this:

1. **Lookup request** \- Send a query with known identifiers (email, LinkedIn URL, name + company)
2. **Entity matching** \- The API matches your query against its database using probabilistic matching algorithms
3. **Profile assembly** \- The system combines data from multiple sources into a single unified profile
4. **Response delivery** \- You receive structured JSON with the enriched profile data

Some providers also offer webhook-based monitoring. You register profiles you want to track, and the API pushes notifications when something changes - a job title update, a company switch, a new email address. This is especially valuable for recruiting teams tracking passive candidates who aren't actively looking but might become open to outreach after a role change.

### How These APIs Compare to Other Recruiting Tools

The recruiting data landscape has three distinct tool categories, and they serve different users:

- **Recruiting data APIs** (this guide) - for developers building recruiting tools or enriching databases programmatically
- [**People search APIs**](https://www.pin.com/blog/best-people-search-apis/?ref=pin-com.ghost.io) \- a subset focused specifically on person-level lookups and search queries
- [**Contact finder tools**](https://www.pin.com/blog/contact-finder-tools-recruiters/?ref=pin-com.ghost.io) \- end-user products (not APIs) that surface emails and phone numbers through a browser extension or web app
- **Full recruiting platforms** \- tools like Pin that combine candidate data, outreach, and scheduling into one workflow, eliminating the need for separate API integrations

## Why Do Recruiting Teams Need Profile Data APIs?

About 70% of organizations report challenges filling full-time positions, according to [SHRM's 2025 Talent Trends](https://www.shrm.org/topics-tools/research/2025-talent-trends/recruiting?ref=pin-com.ghost.io) research. A major contributor to that difficulty? Stale candidate data. B2B contact data decays at roughly 2% per month - meaning nearly one in four records goes invalid within a year, per HubSpot's B2B data quality benchmarks.

For a recruiting team managing 10,000 candidate records in their ATS, that's approximately 2,500 dead contacts by year-end. Outreach emails bounce. Phone numbers disconnect. Job titles are outdated by two positions. The result: wasted sourcing time, poor response rates, and a pipeline that looks full but performs empty.

![How Fast Candidate Data Decays (at 2%/month)](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Recruiting data APIs address this by providing continuously refreshed data that recruiting teams can pull on demand. Instead of relying on a static database export that goes stale the moment it's downloaded, teams query the API for current information at the point of outreach or when enriching ATS records.

### Five Core Use Cases for Recruiting

Here's how recruiting teams and HR tech developers actually use these enrichment APIs:

1. **ATS record enrichment** \- When a candidate applies or gets added to the pipeline, the API auto-fills missing fields: current employer, direct email, phone number, skills, and education
2. **Sourcing from scratch** \- Querying the API with filters (title, location, industry, skills, company size) to build targeted candidate lists without manual searching
3. **Database re-enrichment** \- Running stale ATS records through the API to update job titles, emails, and employer information before launching [outreach campaigns](https://www.pin.com/blog/recruiting-email-templates/?ref=pin-com.ghost.io)
4. **Job change monitoring** \- Setting up webhook-based alerts that notify you when a tracked candidate changes roles - the optimal window for outreach
5. **AI agent data layer** \- Feeding real-time profile data to AI recruiting agents so they can autonomously source, score, and draft personalized outreach

That fifth use case is accelerating fast. Some 64% of organizations used AI in recruiting in 2025, according to [SHRM](https://www.shrm.org/executive-network/insights/people-strategy/state-of-recruiting-2025-insights-to-maximize-recruitment?ref=pin-com.ghost.io). AI adoption in HR tasks specifically jumped from 26% to 43% between 2024 and 2025, per [SHRM's Talent Trends](https://www.shrm.org/topics-tools/research/2025-talent-trends/ai-in-hr?ref=pin-com.ghost.io) data. As more recruiting workflows become AI-driven, the APIs feeding those systems with candidate data become critical infrastructure.

## How Should You Evaluate a Profile Data API?

The five criteria that matter most for recruiting use cases are coverage, data freshness, compliance posture, pricing structure, and technical integration complexity. Not all enrichment APIs are equal. Whether you're integrating a recruiting data API into an HR tech product or comparing vendor solutions as a talent team, these criteria determine what actually works in production. Some providers focus on volume (billions of records, many outdated). Others prioritize accuracy (smaller databases, human-verified). Here's the evaluation framework that matters for recruiting use cases.

### Database Coverage

Coverage means two things: total number of profiles and geographic distribution. People Data Labs leads on raw volume with 1.5B+ individual profiles across 180+ countries. ZoomInfo claims 321M active professionals - a smaller total but more aggressively maintained. For recruiting teams focused on North America and Europe, geographic depth within those regions matters more than global totals.

Ask these questions when evaluating coverage:

- How many profiles are in my target geography?
- What percentage of profiles include email addresses? Phone numbers?
- How frequently are profiles updated?
- What's the coverage for my target job functions and seniority levels?

### Data Freshness

Given 2% monthly decay, freshness is arguably the most important evaluation criterion. Ask providers: how often do you re-crawl and update profiles? What's the median age of records in your database? Do you offer real-time enrichment (query at lookup time) or only batch-processed data (refreshed on a fixed schedule)?

Providers that re-crawl weekly or offer real-time lookup tend to deliver significantly better accuracy than those running monthly batch processes. The difference shows up directly in outreach bounce rates.

### Compliance Posture

After Proxycurl's shutdown and a string of GDPR fines in 2024-2025, compliance has moved from "nice to have" to "existential risk." We'll cover the legal landscape in detail below, but during evaluation you need to ask:

- How do you source your data? (Public scraping, data partnerships, user contributions?)
- Do you maintain GDPR-compliant data processing agreements?
- How do you handle opt-out and deletion requests?
- Have you faced any legal action from LinkedIn, Meta, or other platforms?

### Pricing Structure

Data API pricing falls into three models: per-credit (pay for each lookup), subscription tiers (fixed monthly fee with usage limits), and enterprise contracts (annual commitments with custom terms). The right model depends on your query volume and use pattern. Low-volume users benefit from per-credit pricing. High-volume production systems need flat-rate or enterprise agreements to control costs.

## Self-Serve Recruiting Data API Providers

These providers offer API access through self-serve signups, published pricing, and developer documentation you can start using within hours. They're the right fit for small-to-mid-size recruiting teams, independent HR tech developers, and anyone who needs programmatic access without a sales call.

### People Data Labs

The largest dedicated candidate data API. People Data Labs (PDL) indexes 1.5B+ individual profiles and 62.1M company records across 180+ countries. Their API supports enrichment (pass an email, get back a full profile), search (query by title, skills, location, company), and identify (match partial data points to a person).

**Pricing:** Free tier with 100 lookups/month. Pro starts at $98/mo (350 enrichment credits). Per-credit cost ranges from $0.28 down to $0.20 at volume. Enterprise plans start around $2,500/mo.

**Good for:** Developers building recruiting products who need the largest possible dataset with flexible query options. The API documentation is thorough, and the free tier lets you prototype before committing.

### Apollo.io

Originally a sales engagement platform, Apollo.io has grown into a hybrid data + outreach tool with 275M+ contacts and 30M company profiles. The API covers person enrichment, company enrichment, and people search.

**Pricing:** Basic plan starts at $49/user/month (annual billing). Full API access requires the Organization tier at $119/user/month. The lower tiers provide limited API functionality.

**Good for:** Teams that want data enrichment and outreach in one platform. The catch: API access is gated behind the higher-priced tier, and the database skews toward sales contacts rather than passive technical talent.

### RocketReach

RocketReach indexes 700M+ professional profiles and 60M companies. The API supports person lookup, company lookup, and search. It integrates with Salesforce and Bullhorn, making it useful for recruiting teams already running those systems.

**Pricing:** Essentials starts at $33.25/month (annual billing) for basic lookups. Full API access requires the Ultimate plan at $2,099/year. No free tier for API usage.

**Good for:** Mid-market recruiting teams that need a solid contact database with CRM integrations. Database size is large, though accuracy varies by region.

### Lusha

Lusha offers 100M+ business profiles and 15M companies with a focus on direct-dial phone numbers and verified emails. The free tier (40 credits/month) lets you test data quality before upgrading.

**Pricing:** Free (40 credits/month). Pro starts at $22.45/user/month (annual). API access is an add-on only available on the Scale plan (custom pricing).

**Good for:** Small recruiting teams that need a low-cost entry point for contact data. The free tier is generous enough for light usage. The limitation: API access isn't available on lower plans, so you're using the browser extension, not building integrations.

### Coresignal

Coresignal specializes in professional network data and job posting datasets. Rather than just providing contact details, they focus on workforce signals: hiring surges, layoff patterns, company growth indicators, and employee count trends.

**Pricing:** Starter at $49/month (250 Collect credits). Pro at $800/month. Premium at $1,500/month. API access is included in all paid plans.

**Good for:** HR tech developers building signal-based recruiting products. If you need to detect when a company is scaling (or contracting) to time your outreach, Coresignal's data is more useful than a static contact database.

### Hunter.io and Snov.io

Both are email-focused enrichment tools with API access. Hunter.io covers 200M contacts across 130M companies, with daily database updates and confidence scoring on email accuracy. Snov.io bundles email finding with outreach sequences, making it a lightweight alternative to heavier recruiting platforms.

**Pricing:** Hunter.io Pro S starts at $99/month (5,000 credits). Snov.io starts at $39/month (1,000 credits) with a free tier (50 credits). Both include API access on all paid plans.

**Good for:** Teams that primarily need email enrichment rather than full profile data. If your main goal is validating and finding email addresses at scale, these are more cost-effective than full-profile API providers. For a deeper comparison of email-specific tools, see our [email finder tools guide](https://www.pin.com/blog/best-email-finder-tools-recruiters/?ref=pin-com.ghost.io).

## Enterprise Data API Providers

Enterprise providers require sales conversations, annual contracts, and typically five-figure minimum commitments. They're built for large recruiting operations, staffing firms with high-volume needs, and companies where data compliance requires vendor-managed controls.

### ZoomInfo

ZoomInfo is the incumbent giant with 321M active professional profiles and 104M company records. Their TalentOS product is purpose-built for recruiting, offering intent data, org charts, and hiring signals alongside standard contact enrichment.

**Pricing:** Starts around $15,000/year for platform access. API enrichment add-ons begin at roughly $5,000/year. Full TalentOS implementations often exceed $40,000/year. No self-serve option.

**Caveat:** The pricing opacity is intentional - ZoomInfo's contracts are highly negotiable, which means published numbers are starting points. The platform is powerful but expensive, and most SMB recruiting teams will find better value elsewhere.

### Cognism

Cognism indexes 400M+ contacts with a strong European skew - making it particularly relevant for teams recruiting across EU markets. Their Diamond Data subset includes phone-verified direct dials, which commands a premium but delivers higher connect rates.

**Pricing:** Platform fee ranges from $15,000-$25,000/year plus per-seat costs. A 5-user Grow plan runs approximately $22,500/year. Enterprise plans exceed $37,500/year.

**Caveat:** Cognism's GDPR compliance posture is one of the strongest in the market - they're GDPR-certified and have built their European data collection specifically around Article 6(1)(f) legitimate interest. But you're paying for that compliance assurance. The per-seat model also makes costs unpredictable as teams grow.

### FullContact and Pipl

FullContact focuses on identity resolution - matching fragmented data points across multiple sources into a unified person record. Pricing starts at approximately $99/month for Essentials, scaling to $6,000-$83,000/year on contracts.

Pipl specializes in identity verification with 3B+ identities and 25B+ individual records cross-referenced. Pricing runs approximately $0.10/query at default limits, with contracts ranging from $3,000 to $130,000/year.

**Caveat:** Neither tool is primarily designed for recruiting. FullContact serves adtech and marketing use cases. Pipl serves fraud prevention and background checks. Both can supplement a recruiting data stack, but they shouldn't be your primary candidate enrichment source.

Pin's AI scans 850M+ profiles to find candidates with recruiter-level precision - [**try it free**](https://www.pin.com/?ref=pin-com.ghost.io).

## Pricing Compared: All 12 Data API Providers

Pricing is the single most confusing aspect of this market. Some providers charge per-credit, others per-seat, others per-query, and some combine all three. Here's a consolidated comparison to cut through the noise:

| Provider | Starting Price | Free Tier | API Access Threshold | Database Size |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| People Data Labs | $98/mo | Yes (100 lookups/mo) | Pro tier | 1.5B+ profiles |
| Apollo.io | $49/user/mo | Yes (limited credits) | Organization ($119/user/mo) | 275M+ contacts |
| RocketReach | $33.25/mo | No | Ultimate ($2,099/yr) | 700M+ profiles |
| Lusha | $22.45/user/mo | Yes (40 credits/mo) | Scale plan (custom) | 100M+ profiles |
| Coresignal | $49/mo | No | All paid plans | Workforce signal data |

| ZoomInfo | ~$15,000/yr | No | Custom add-on (~$5K/yr) | 321M professionals |
| Cognism | ~$22,500/yr (5 users) | No | Included in enterprise | 400M+ contacts |
| FullContact | ~$99/mo | No | Must contact sales | Not disclosed |
| Pipl | ~$0.10/query | No | Must contact sales | 3B+ identities |
| **Pin (no API needed)** | **$100/mo** | **Yes (no credit card)** | **N/A - built-in UI** | **850M+ profiles** |

Notice the pricing gap. Self-serve API providers cluster between $39-$99/month for basic access. Enterprise providers jump to $15,000-$50,000+/year. There's almost nothing in between - which is exactly why platforms like Pin exist. You get access to one of the largest candidate databases (850M+ profiles) without building API integrations or signing enterprise contracts.

## What Market Shifts Are Reshaping Profile Data APIs?

The data enrichment market in 2026 looks fundamentally different from even two years ago. Three events have redefined the landscape.

### 1\. The Proxycurl Shutdown

Proxycurl was a popular developer-friendly API that made LinkedIn profile data accessible via simple REST calls. It generated roughly $10M in annual recurring revenue. Then LinkedIn filed a lawsuit in January 2025, alleging Proxycurl operated hundreds of thousands of fake accounts to scrape member data, according to [LinkedIn's official announcement](https://news.linkedin.com/2025/linkedin-takes-legal-action-to-defend-member-privacy?ref=pin-com.ghost.io).

The result was swift. Proxycurl settled, agreed to permanently delete all LinkedIn data, and shut down entirely on July 4, 2025. The founder pivoted to an unrelated product. For developers who had built recruiting tools on Proxycurl's API, this was a wake-up call: any data provider that depends on fake accounts or unauthorized access to collect data carries existential legal risk.

The lesson isn't that these APIs are inherently risky. It's that the collection method matters enormously. Providers that scrape publicly visible data without authentication (the approach Bright Data uses) have been legally validated. Providers that create fake accounts to access gated data have been consistently shut down.

### 2\. Clearbit's Absorption into HubSpot

Clearbit was the go-to free enrichment API for early-stage companies and bootstrapped developers. HubSpot acquired Clearbit in 2023, and by April 30, 2025, all standalone free Clearbit tools were sunset. The enrichment functionality now lives inside HubSpot Breeze Intelligence, requiring a paid HubSpot subscription plus credits.

This migration stranded thousands of developers who had built lightweight integrations on Clearbit's free webhook. Many have moved to People Data Labs (similar API design, free tier available) or Apollo.io (combines data with outreach tools).

### 3\. LinkedIn's Legal Offensive

LinkedIn has escalated enforcement against data scrapers. Beyond Proxycurl, LinkedIn filed suit against ProAPIs in October 2025, alleging millions of fake accounts used to collect and sell scraped data for up to $15,000/month, as reported by [The Record](https://therecord.media/linkedin-sues-data-scraping-company?ref=pin-com.ghost.io). The case reportedly settled in early 2026.

But here's the nuance: the courts have consistently held that scraping publicly accessible data doesn't violate the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act. The hiQ Labs v. LinkedIn case - which went to the Supreme Court and back before settling in December 2022 - established that the CFAA doesn't apply to public-facing web data. What gets providers in trouble is the use of fake accounts, not the act of scraping itself.

The Meta v. Bright Data case in January 2024 reinforced this distinction. A federal judge ruled that Meta's Terms of Service doesn't prohibit scraping data that's publicly visible to logged-out users. Meta dropped the case the following month.

## How Does Compliance Apply to Profile Data APIs?

Compliance isn't optional in 2026. The combination of GDPR enforcement in Europe, expanding CCPA penalties in the US, and LinkedIn's legal strategy means every team using data APIs needs to understand the regulatory boundaries.

### GDPR Requirements

In the European Union, "publicly accessible" data is not automatically GDPR-compliant to collect and process. You still need a lawful basis, typically Article 6(1)(f) legitimate interest. This means conducting a documented Legitimate Interest Assessment (LIA), ensuring data subjects can exercise their rights (access, deletion, objection), and demonstrating proportionality - the business need must justify the privacy impact.

France's data protection authority (CNIL) fined KASPR approximately $240,000 in December 2024 specifically for scraping LinkedIn contact details without adequate legal basis. The maximum GDPR penalty is 20 million euros or 4% of global annual revenue - whichever is higher.

When evaluating API providers for EU recruiting, ask: do they maintain GDPR-compliant data processing agreements? How do they handle right-to-erasure requests? Do they have documented LIAs for their data collection practices? Cognism, for example, has built their entire EU data collection specifically around GDPR compliance - which partially explains their higher pricing.

### CCPA and US State Privacy Laws

In the US, CCPA penalties increased on January 1, 2025 to $2,663 per unintentional violation and $7,988 per intentional violation, according to the [California Privacy Protection Agency](https://cppa.ca.gov/announcements/2024/20241217.html?ref=pin-com.ghost.io). More importantly, the CPPA levied a $1.35M fine against Tractor Supply in 2025 - the first published CCPA enforcement action specifically covering job applicant data, as reported by the [National Law Review](https://natlawreview.com/article/california-privacy-protection-agency-levies-record-135-million-fine?ref=pin-com.ghost.io).

Employment-related privacy enforcement has expanded significantly. California, Colorado, and Connecticut announced collaborative enforcement in September 2025, meaning violations can trigger multi-state investigations simultaneously. If your recruiting team uses profile data APIs to collect candidate information on US individuals, you need CCPA-compliant data handling processes - not just from your API provider, but in your own systems.

### The Legal Bright Line: Public Data vs. Fake Accounts

Here's the rule that matters most for evaluating profile data API providers: scraping publicly visible data is legal. Creating fake accounts to access gated data is not. Every major court decision in 2022-2025 has reinforced this distinction:

- **hiQ v. LinkedIn** (settled Dec 2022) - CFAA doesn't prohibit scraping public data; fake accounts cross the line
- **Meta v. Bright Data** (Jan 2024) - Terms of Service can't prohibit scraping of logged-out-visible data
- **LinkedIn v. Proxycurl** (settled 2025) - Fake accounts = shutdown and data destruction
- **LinkedIn v. ProAPIs** (filed Oct 2025) - Millions of fake accounts alleged

When evaluating a provider, ask directly: how do you collect your data? If they can't clearly explain their collection methodology - or if their pricing seems too good for their claimed database size - that's a red flag.

## How Do You Build a Profile Data Strategy?

The right approach depends on whether you're building a custom data pipeline (developers integrating a recruiting data API into an HR tech product) or selecting a managed platform (talent teams who need candidate data without engineering overhead). Knowing which APIs exist and how compliance works is useful, but it's only half the decision.

### For Developers Building Recruiting Products

If you're building an HR tech product that needs profile data as infrastructure, start with People Data Labs or Coresignal for development (both have free or low-cost entry points). Design your system to support multiple data providers from the start - single-provider dependency is the lesson Proxycurl's customers learned the hard way.

Implement these architectural patterns:

- **Provider abstraction layer** \- Wrap API calls behind your own interface so you can swap providers without changing application code
- **Hybrid enrichment** \- Use batch processing for baseline database maintenance and real-time queries at the point of user interaction
- **Data freshness scoring** \- Track the last-enriched date for each profile and prioritize re-enrichment for records approaching your staleness threshold
- **Compliance-by-default** \- Log the data source, collection date, and legal basis for every profile record from day one

For a detailed comparison of specific APIs, including response formats and integration examples, see our [developer guide to people search APIs](https://www.pin.com/blog/best-people-search-apis/?ref=pin-com.ghost.io).

### For Recruiting Teams That Need Data Now

Most recruiting teams don't need to build API integrations. They need candidate data, contact information, and outreach tools that work together. Building a custom data pipeline from profile data APIs requires developer resources, ongoing maintenance, and compliance infrastructure that most recruiting operations can't justify.

The more practical path: use a platform that has already integrated the data layer. Pin, for example, gives recruiters access to 850M+ candidate profiles with built-in contact lookup, multi-channel outreach (email, LinkedIn, SMS), and [automated outreach sequences](https://www.pin.com/blog/automated-candidate-outreach/?ref=pin-com.ghost.io) that deliver a 48% response rate - all in a single interface starting at $100/month.

As Nick Poloni, President at Cascadia Search Group, put it: "The sourcing data is incredible, scanning 850M+ profiles with recruiter-level precision to uncover perfect-fit candidates I'd never find otherwise. Best of all, the outreach feels genuinely personalized and non-generic, driving sky-high reply rates where candidates even thank me for the thoughtful messages."

The question isn't whether profile data APIs are valuable - they are. It's whether your team should be the one integrating, maintaining, and monitoring them. For developers building recruiting products: absolutely. For recruiters trying to fill roles: skip the API layer and use a platform that's already done the integration work.

### Real-Time vs. Batch Enrichment

The industry has moved decisively toward real-time enrichment. Here's why: AI-powered recruiting agents need current context to operate accurately. A batch-processed database refreshed monthly creates "stale data windows" where an agent might draft outreach to someone who changed jobs three weeks ago.

The recommended approach is a hybrid model:

- **Batch processing** \- Run monthly or quarterly sweeps across your full ATS database to catch stale records and update baseline information
- **Real-time enrichment** \- Query at the point of interaction: when a recruiter opens a candidate profile, when an AI agent drafts outreach, or when a candidate enters a new pipeline stage
- **Event-triggered enrichment** \- Use webhook monitoring to catch job changes, funding announcements, and hiring signals that create optimal outreach windows

This hybrid model balances cost (batch is cheaper per query) with accuracy (real-time catches changes that batch misses). Most self-serve API providers support both modes.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Profile data API vs. people search engine: what's the difference?

A profile data API returns structured candidate data (JSON payloads with job titles, employment history, contact details) that software can process programmatically. A people search engine provides a user interface for manual searches. APIs are for developers building tools; search engines are for recruiters doing hands-on sourcing. Platforms like [AI candidate sourcing tools](https://www.pin.com/blog/ai-candidate-sourcing/?ref=pin-com.ghost.io) combine both capabilities.

### How much do profile data APIs cost for recruiting use cases?

Self-serve profile data APIs range from $39/month (Snov.io) to $98/month (People Data Labs). Enterprise providers like ZoomInfo and Cognism start at $15,000-$22,500/year. Full API access often requires higher tiers - Apollo.io gates API access behind its $119/user/month Organization plan. For recruiter-ready access without API integration, Pin starts at $100/month with a free tier.

### Is it legal to use profile data APIs that scrape LinkedIn?

Courts have consistently ruled that scraping publicly accessible data doesn't violate the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (hiQ v. LinkedIn, settled 2022; Meta v. Bright Data, 2024). What's illegal: creating fake accounts to access gated data. Proxycurl was shut down in 2025 specifically for operating fake accounts, not for scraping. Always verify your provider's collection methodology - public data is defensible, fake accounts are not.

### Which profile data API has the largest database?

Pipl claims the largest at 3B+ identities, though it's focused on identity verification rather than recruiting. For recruiting-specific use cases, People Data Labs leads with 1.5B+ individual profiles across 180+ countries. RocketReach (700M+ profiles) and Cognism (400M+ contacts) are the next largest. For recruiters, Pin offers 850M+ profiles with 100% coverage in North America and Europe - no API required.

### What happened to Proxycurl and Clearbit?

Proxycurl shut down on July 4, 2025 after LinkedIn sued for operating hundreds of thousands of fake accounts. The company had approximately $10M in annual revenue. Clearbit was acquired by HubSpot in 2023, and all standalone free tools were sunset by April 30, 2025. Clearbit's enrichment now lives inside HubSpot Breeze Intelligence, requiring a paid HubSpot subscription. Developers who built on either platform have largely migrated to People Data Labs or Apollo.io.

## Which Profile Data API Should You Choose?

Profile data APIs serve a real and growing need. The data enrichment market is on track to nearly double by 2030. AI adoption in recruiting is accelerating. And candidate data decay makes continuous enrichment a necessity, not a luxury.

But the market is also getting more complex - legally, technically, and commercially. Choosing the wrong provider (or building on a legally vulnerable one) can mean more than wasted engineering time. It can mean shut down access, deleted data, and a compliance liability.

Here's the decision framework:

- **Building an HR tech product?** Start with People Data Labs (largest dataset, developer-friendly, free tier). Design for multi-provider support from day one.
- **Need enrichment for a mid-size ATS?** Apollo.io or RocketReach give you data + integrations without enterprise pricing.
- **Recruiting in the EU?** Cognism's GDPR-certified posture is worth the premium if European compliance is a hard requirement.
- **Just need to find and reach candidates?** Skip the API layer entirely. [Pin](https://www.pin.com/?ref=pin-com.ghost.io) gives you 850M+ profiles, contact lookup, multi-channel outreach, and interview scheduling in one platform - starting free with no credit card required.

[Skip to content](https://coefficient.io/top-data-enrichment-apis#primary) Last Modified: September 29, 2025 - 23 min read Nikesh Vora Join our community [![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/yt-icon.svg)](https://www.youtube.com/@coefficientio "YouTube")[![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/twitter-icon.svg)](https://twitter.com/coefficient_io "Twitter")[![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/fb-icon.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/Coefficient.io "Facebook")[![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/linkedin-icon.svg)](https://www.linkedin.com/company/coefficientworks "LinkedIn") Missing data kills deals. Your CRM has gaps. Your emails bounce. Your calls go nowhere. **Data enrichment APIs** fix this by filling in the blanks automatically—turning partial contacts into complete profiles ready for outreach. Let’s explore the best free and paid **data enrichment APIs** that transform incomplete data into actionable intelligence. ## **Feature Comparison Table** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link | | | | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Tool** | **Pricing Model** | **Data Coverage** | **API Rate Limits** | **Key Data Points** | **Compliance** | **Best For** | | **Hunter.io** | Free: 50/mo
Paid: $34-$349/mo | North America, Europe | 300 requests/min | Email, verification | GDPR compliant | Email finding | | **Apollo.io** | Free: 100 credits/mo
Paid: $49-$149/user | 210M+ contacts | 400 profiles/hour | Email, phone, firmographics | GDPR, CCPA | All-in-one sales | | **FullContact** | $99-$10,000+/mo | Global | Enterprise-grade | 700+ insights | GDPR, CCPA | Identity resolution | | **Snov.io** | Free: 50 credits
Paid: $39-$99/mo | Global | Standard | Email, LinkedIn | GDPR compliant | Multichannel outreach | | **Lusha** | Free: 40 credits/mo
Paid: $29-$69/mo | 1.5M+ users | Standard | Phone, email | GDPR compliant | Direct dials | | **ZoomInfo API** | $12,000+/year | 200M+ contacts | Enterprise | Full profile data | SOC 2 Type II | Enterprise teams | | **Apollo.io Pro** | $1,000+/mo | 210M+ contacts | 250,000/mo | Tech stack, intent | GDPR, CCPA | Scale operations | | **People Data Labs** | Free: 100/mo
Paid: $98+/mo | 3.1B+ profiles | Flexible | Full demographics | GDPR, CCPA | Developers | | **Proxycurl** | $10-$199/mo | Real-time | Standard | LinkedIn profiles | Standard | Fresh data | | **Lusha Premium** | $3,000+/mo | Premium coverage | 250,000/mo | Intent scores | Enhanced | High volume | | **Coresignal** | $49-$1,500+/mo | 792M+ records | Enterprise | Historical data | Standard | Market research | | **EnrichmentAPI** | $0.005/call | Basic coverage | Per-call | Core fields | Standard | Simple needs | | **Breeze Intelligence** | $45-$900/mo | HubSpot only | 50,000/mo | 40+ data points | HubSpot native | HubSpot users | [![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/badge-auto-cta-icon-blue.svg)\\ \\ Did you know? Coefficient eliminates the need to export data manually and rebuild stale dashboards. Get started by pulling live data into pre-built Sheets dashboards.](https://coefficient.io/get-started?ref=blog) ## [**Hunter.io**](http://hunter.io/) ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link Hunter.io turns company domains into verified email addresses, making it simple for sales teams to find and reach decision-makers. The platform combines email discovery with verification and campaign tools, creating a complete outreach solution that works directly from your browser or API. ### **Highlights of Hunter.io** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link - Database with strong North American and European coverage - Chrome extension for instant LinkedIn email discovery - All-in-one platform with email campaigns and CRM features - Bulk processing for large domain lists ### **Pros** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link - **Simple to start:** The interface needs zero training. Your team can find emails immediately without watching tutorials or reading guides. - **Complete outreach toolkit:** Beyond finding emails, Hunter.io manages campaigns, verifies addresses, and runs automated sequences. One tool replaces three or four separate subscriptions. - **Strong integrations:** The API connects with Salesforce, HubSpot, and Pipedrive. Zapier support means you can automate workflows without coding. ### **Cons** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link - **Accuracy dropping:** Email finding accuracy fell to 65-75% this year. That’s a 12% decline. Your cost per verified lead now exceeds $3-5. - **Weak international data:** Coverage drops hard outside North America and Western Europe. Asian and African markets show particularly poor accuracy rates. - **Pricey for small teams:** The free plan’s 50 monthly searches disappear fast. Paid plans start at $49/month, which hurts small businesses needing volume. ### **Pricing** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link As of February 2025, Hunter.io offers a free plan with 50 searches monthly. Paid plans: Starter at $49/month (monthly) or $34/month (annual), Growth at $149/month or $104/month annually, and Business at $499/month or $349/month annually. ### **What do users say about Hunter.io?** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link **Positive Review:** “Hunter is cost-effective, makes it incredibly easy to automate cold-email campaigns and is simply so easy to use. I never have to train my team on Hunter, and they already have so much material on how to use it well anyway! It has incredible integrations and the team are always actively developing and extending the platform.” **Critical Review:** “Before hunter looking for emails and industry-insights was incredibly manual and time consuming, hunter has sped up our market research significantly. However, it would be great to have something like a JetPack CRM or Suite CRM plugin, but naturally we can use the API for this anyhow.” ### **Support** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link Hunter.io provides email support at contact@hunter.io, plus a Help Center with 92+ FAQ articles. Higher-tier plans get priority support. The team focuses on fast responses, empathy, and detailed answers through weekly success meetings and pair-support sessions. ## [**Apollo.io**](http://apollo.io/) ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link Apollo.io merges prospecting, outreach, and CRM into one platform that handles your entire sales process. With access to millions of B2B contacts and built-in engagement tools, it eliminates the need for multiple sales tools while providing everything from lead generation to deal closing. ### **Highlights of Apollo.io** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link - Most-reviewed G2 product with 8,800+ reviews and 4.7/5 rating - 183 No. 1 rankings in G2’s Summer 2025 Report - Lead generation, CRM, email sequences, and phone dialer combined - Chrome extension for LinkedIn prospecting ### **Pros** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link - **Everything in one place:** Apollo combines lead capture, CRM, email sequences, and sales intelligence. No more juggling multiple tools. Your software costs drop immediately. - **Massive database:** The platform maintains extensive contact and company data. Small to medium businesses get particularly good coverage, plus real-time enrichment. - **Users love it:** With 183 #1 rankings on G2, Apollo proves its value daily. User satisfaction stays consistently high across thousands of reviews. ### **Cons** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link - **Credit math confusion:** Different actions eat different credit amounts. Eight credits for a phone number. Multiple credits for enrichment. Predicting monthly costs becomes impossible. - **Free plan gutted:** New accounts get 100 monthly email credits. Legacy accounts still receive 10,000. The free tier lost most of its value. - **Interface overload:** Users call it “tough to figure out.” The platform packs so many features that new users struggle to find value initially. ### **Pricing** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link As of February 2025, Apollo offers: Free plan with 100 credits monthly, Basic at $49/month per user (annual) or $59/month (monthly), Professional at $99/month per user (annual), and Organization at $149/month per user (minimum 3 users, annual only). ### **What do users say about Apollo.io?** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link **Positive Review:** “Apollo makes it really easy to find accurate contact information and build targeted lead lists. I also like how seamlessly it integrates with email sequences, the sequences are a huge help for our business and they are easy to implement and track. Generally Customer support is very solid, going out of their way to help us set-up our business.” **Critical Review:** “Apollo.io changed their UI and added more limitations to the free tier. Now, you need 1 credit to save a verified email contact to your list, and the same goes for phone numbers. The free plan is now useless compared to what it used to be.” ### **Support** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link Apollo.io provides email support, live chat, and phone support for higher tiers. The platform offers comprehensive documentation, video tutorials, and regular webinars. Users consistently praise the responsive support team who “go out of their way to help” with setup and issues. ## **FullContact** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link FullContact specializes in identity resolution, unifying customer data across email, social media, phone, and other touchpoints into single profiles. The platform enriches contacts with detailed demographic, social, and behavioral insights while maintaining enterprise-grade privacy compliance. ### **Highlights of FullContact** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link - Identity resolution unifying profiles across channels - Cross-channel engagement capabilities - 700+ behavioral insights with 85% match rates - Built-in GDPR and CCPA compliance ### **Pros** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link - **True identity resolution:** FullContact excels at connecting fragmented data across channels. You get a real 360-degree customer view by unifying scattered information. - **Deep enrichment data:** The platform provides extensive demographic, social, and behavioral insights. These details help personalize every customer interaction. - **Enterprise-ready features:** Robust privacy tools, enterprise security, and extensive CRM integrations make FullContact suitable for large organizations with strict requirements. ### **Cons** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link - **Complex pricing maze:** Users call the pricing structure overly complicated. Salespeople push expensive packages that quickly exceed small business budgets. - **Mobile app problems:** The Android app has bugs. Contact synchronization fails. The interface needs constant refreshing to work properly. - **Support struggles:** Support responds but rarely resolves issues. Some users report weeks of back-and-forth without fixing technical problems. ### **Pricing** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link As of February 2025, FullContact starts at $500/month for Basic (small businesses), $2,000/month for Premium (medium businesses), and $10,000+/month for Enterprise. Pay-as-you-go starts at $99/month. Custom enterprise pricing available. ### **What do users say about FullContact?** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link **Positive Review:** “Using FullContact Enrich API, we can get a better picture of a person using their email address. We can get a person’s name, age, gender, city, country, job and a lot more details using the API. This data can be helpful in finding and qualifying leads. I’d highly recommend FullContact to anyone, whether through our platform or by their own integration.” **Critical Review:** “I would avoid this software at all costs. It has wasted time, energy and money for my business and has been detrimental to our sales efforts. When I needed access to our FullContact list from my personal laptop, it automatically synced my personal Google & iCloud contacts as well as personal bank details without permission. FullContact should not sync anything without permission.” ### **Support** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link FullContact offers email support, dedicated account management for higher tiers, and phone support for enterprise customers. The company provides a knowledge base, community forums, and extensive documentation. User reviews show mixed experiences with response times and issue resolution. ## [**Snov.io**](http://snov.io/) ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link Snov.io combines email finding, verification, and multichannel outreach including LinkedIn automation in one platform. The tool serves B2B teams needing lead generation, email marketing, and sales automation with built-in CRM functionality to manage the entire process. ### **Highlights of Snov.io** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link - Multichannel outreach with email and LinkedIn automation - Built-in email warm-up for better deliverability - 24/7 chat support with responsive team - Affordable pricing starting at $39/month ### **Pros** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link - **All-in-one simplicity:** Snov.io combines email finding, verification, campaigns, LinkedIn automation, and CRM. One subscription replaces multiple tools and streamlines workflows. - **Deliverability focus:** Built-in verification, warm-up tools, and deliverability checks maintain sender reputation. Your bounce rates drop while inbox placement improves. - **Support that cares:** Users consistently praise the 24/7 chat support. Quick responses, helpful team members, extensive blog content, and regular training webinars keep customers successful. ### **Cons** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link - **Credit math headaches:** Different actions consume varying credits. Most teams pay 2-3x the base plan once LinkedIn automation and actual credit needs factor in. - **LinkedIn costs extra:** LinkedIn slots cost $69/month each. Multichannel outreach gets expensive fast when you add these required extras. - **Accuracy varies:** Users report inconsistent email finding and verification. The platform sometimes misses obviously invalid addresses that should get caught. ### **Pricing** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link As of February 2025, Snov.io offers: Free trial with 50 credits and 100 recipients, Starter at $39/month (1,000 credits, 5,000 recipients), Pro at $99/month (5,000 credits, 10,000 recipients). Higher tiers available. LinkedIn automation costs extra $69/month per slot. ### **What do users say about Snov.io?** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link **Positive Review:** “What I like best about Snov.io is how clean and easy it is to use. The interface is super modern, so you’re not stuck digging through cluttered menus or outdated layouts—it just feels smooth. Throughout my time using Snov.io, the customer support team was prompt and helpful. Many users have shared their positive experiences with Snov.io, especially praising its easy-to-use interface, accurate email finding, and time-saving automation.” **Critical Review:** “During our month-long test, Snov.io consistently underperformed. The email finder failed one-third of the time. The verification missed obvious bad emails. And don’t get me started on their customer support. Snov.io had potential. Some features worked decently. The interface wasn’t terrible. The pricing seemed reasonable. It just wasn’t reliable enough for serious cold outreach.” ### **Support** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link Snov.io provides 24/7 live chat support and email support at help@snov.io. The platform offers educational resources including a regularly updated blog, webinars, and training sessions. Multiple contact options exist for partnerships and data protection inquiries. ## **Lusha** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link Lusha provides B2B contact data through an easy-to-use platform that delivers email addresses, phone numbers, and company information. Known for simplicity, browser extension functionality, and CRM integrations, it’s particularly popular with sales development teams. ### **Highlights of Lusha** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link - High-quality verified emails and direct phone numbers - Chrome extension for instant LinkedIn prospecting - Simple interface with minimal learning curve - Trusted by 1.5+ million users ### **Pros** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link - **Start immediately:** Lusha’s intuitive interface needs no training. Sales teams begin using the platform instantly without extensive onboarding sessions. - **Direct browser access:** The platform works seamlessly in browsers and integrates with popular CRMs. Enrich leads in clicks without switching tools. - **Compliance first:** Lusha emphasizes data privacy and GDPR compliance. Perfect for businesses in regulated industries or international markets. ### **Cons** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link - **Credit limits hurt:** The Pro plan provides only 250 credits (about 40 leads monthly). Active sales teams burn through credits quickly. - **Costs escalate fast:** Entry pricing looks reasonable. But teams needing more credits, API access, or advanced integrations face significant price jumps. - **Features locked away:** Salesforce integration only comes with the top-tier Scale plan. Smaller teams on budget plans miss key functionality. ### **Pricing** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link As of February 2025, Lusha offers: Free plan with 40 credits monthly, Pro at $29/month per user (annual) or $39/month (monthly) with 250 annual credits, Premium at $51/month per user (annual) or $69.90/month (monthly) with 600 annual credits. Scale plan has custom pricing. ### **What do users say about Lusha?** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link **Positive Review:** “Lusha is one of the easiest data enrichment tools to use. It’s especially helpful for sales teams and marketers who want fast, accurate contact data without the complexity of a large platform. Lusha works directly in your browser, on LinkedIn, or inside your CRM so you can enrich leads and contacts in just a few clicks. It’s simple, reliable, and built for teams that move fast.” **Critical Review:** “The Pro plan might not be ideal for larger companies. The Premium and Scale plans offer more credits for those who need them. Advanced features like technographic filters and CRM integration can only be found in the Scale plan. Some users find the guides easy to follow, while others want more in-depth training.” ### **Support** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link Lusha offers email support through their contact form, plus a help center with documentation organized by topics. Phone support comes with higher-tier plans. The company provides training materials, video tutorials, and maintains a community forum for best practices. ## **ZoomInfo API** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link ZoomInfo API delivers enterprise-grade access to one of the world’s largest B2B databases, providing comprehensive search and enrichment for organizations with serious data needs. The platform combines real-time updates with advanced filtering to help sales teams identify and connect with ideal prospects. ### **Highlights of ZoomInfo API** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link - 150M+ contact profiles and 20M+ companies - Daily data refreshes with bulk enrichment - Customizable schemas and webhooks - SOC 2 Type II compliance ### **Pros** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link - **Massive data coverage:** ZoomInfo maintains comprehensive global reach for prospecting and enrichment. Over 150 million contacts ensure you find who you need. - **Real-time freshness:** Daily refresh and change alerts maintain database quality. Your bounce rates drop significantly compared to monthly-updated competitors. - **Enterprise security:** SOC 2 Type II compliance, SSO, and role-based access control protect sensitive data while meeting corporate requirements. ### **Cons** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link - **Budget killer:** Pricing starts above $10,000 yearly. Small businesses simply can’t afford entry-level access to **data enrichment APIs** at this price point. - **Long-term lock-in:** Annual commitments and high minimums reduce flexibility. You’re tied into contracts regardless of changing needs. - **Complex setup:** Initial configuration and schema mapping require dedicated technical resources. Deployment timelines stretch longer than expected. ### **Pricing** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link As of February 2025, ZoomInfo API plans start at $12,000/year for basic API access with minimum 50,000 records. Enterprise and custom tiers available upon request. ### **What do users say about ZoomInfo API?** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link **Positive Review:** “ZoomInfo’s API allowed us to enrich our entire CRM database in under a week. The data quality and coverage are unmatched, which drastically improved our campaign performance.” **Critical Review:** “The onboarding process was painful—schema mapping took weeks, and hidden fees drove our annual spend up by 20% after the first renewal.” ### **Support** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link ZoomInfo offers dedicated account management for API customers, 24/7 email and phone support, detailed developer documentation, sandbox environments, and regular data quality webinars. ## **Apollo.io Pro** ![](https://coefficient.io/wp-content/themes/coefficient/assets/images/coeff-icons/link-icon.svg)Click to copy link Apollo.io Pro extends the free Apollo API with higher limits, advanced fields, and priority support. EmailName

### Frequently asked questions

- What is data enrichment software?







Data enrichment software enables B2B marketing & revenue teams to enrich first-party company and person data in their primary sales and marketing databases (CRMs, marketing automation platforms, CDPs, etc.). This can include updating incorrect or out-of-date data, or adding missing or incomplete data to customer records (customer enrichment) or lead records (lead enrichment). Data enrichment software helps its users better understand customers, create more accurate segments and reporting, and power more precise workflows across the entire funnel.

- What are the benefits of data enrichment software?







Data enrichment software ensures B2B marketing & revenue teams have complete records and up-to-date contact information within their primary databases, from CRMs and marketing automation platforms (MAPs) to customer data platforms (CDPs) and others. And because CRMs, MAPs, and CDPs are responsible for feeding data into other B2B tools, entire technology stacks can benefit from improved data quality. Every tool immediately enables more precise targeting, analytics, and workflows.

- How does data enrichment software work?







Data enrichment software offers two primary capabilities: data sourcing and data enrichment. Data sourcing is the process of collecting, sorting, and verifying millions of third-party company and person data points via hundreds of public and private data sources. Data enrichment is the process of instantly appending those rich third-party data points to a company’s new or existing records.

Boost your company data with instant enrichment

Our Company Enrichment API helps you retrieve unique insights from our company dataset.

On-demand access

Control how you pay

Fresh data

Every record you get back is the most up-to-date version we have in our dataset, refreshed each month.

Built to scale

How it works

Specify the profile you want

Find the best match from our Company Dataset

We will intelligently find the best matching record in the Person Dataset based on your inputs.

API returns the full profile of the best matching record

You get back the entire profile or just the fields you want.
